comment: fleet-ship engine routing - edit lanes freely; the orchestrator reads this at fleet start and on any steering sentence. Interactive shell aliases: xx='codex --yolo', cc='claude --dangerously-skip-permissions', aa='agy --dangerously-skip-permissions' (pass the expanded flags after '--' to 'herdr agent start --kind <codex|claude|agy>'). Resolution order: user sentence override (run ledger) > this file > the skill's built-in table.

lanes.match: Required cross-engine tandem review of routine tasks: PR diffs, chunk commits, plans, reports, and user-facing copy. Escalate reactor-subtle, security-critical, architecture-spec, hold:human, high-stakes copy, or disputed tiebreak reviews to review-hard. Preserve additional technical review requirements.
lanes.argv: use reviewers[builder engine] in order ('gemini' aliases 'agy'); verify model and independence; record unavailable fallback
lanes.reason: Prefer independent Gemini 4 Argon at medium effort (per owner 2026-10-30, gemini-4-argon-medium is the routine review default so Argon high is not overused; escalate to review-hard when stakes warrant). If unavailable or same-engine, use frontier Codex (gpt-6-astra) or Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from another engine. Pin and verify model identity. Lightweight models (gemini-3.8-flash-*, claude-haiku-5-5, gpt-6-luna, mini) never satisfy required review. Worker cost limits do not reduce review quality. Preserve findings across fallback and require consensus; block if no eligible frontier reviewer is available.
lanes.origin: user 2026-10-28 & 2026-10-30: Argon-first cross-engine review; medium default for routine review, high reserved for hard review; no lightweight reviewers

lanes.match: Hard or high-stakes cross-engine tandem review: reactor-subtle diffs, security-critical code, architecture/design specs, hold:human merges, high-stakes copy, and disputed review tiebreaks.
lanes.argv: use reviewers[builder engine] in order ('gemini' aliases 'agy'); verify model and independence; record unavailable fallback
lanes.reason: Reserve gemini-4-argon-high (with high-effort gpt-6-astra, medium-effort claude-fable-5-1, or high-effort claude-opus-5-5 fallbacks) for reviews where deeper multi-step reasoning catches subtle concurrency, security, or architectural defects worth the extra latency and quota.
lanes.origin: user 2026-10-30: reserve Argon high for hard review or high-stakes work

lanes.match: Design plans, implementation plans, wave/architecture planning, and spec/design-document authoring. Takes precedence over frontier and judgment for planning work.
lanes.reason: Use GPT-6-Astra explicitly at high effort for design and architecture plans (plan quality sets downstream chunk boundaries across the wave; never pin max). Do not substitute Opus or Fable for planning without a new user instruction.
lanes.origin: user 2026-09-08: use astra for design plans from now on, update fleet routing

lanes.match: Copywriting, UX writing, microcopy, onboarding/paywall strings, routine store/marketing copy, release notes, outreach drafts, and tone-sensitive reports.
lanes.reason: Gemini 4 Argon excels at natural voice and human-touch prose. Medium effort is the default because copy tone and clarity come from Argon's base voice rather than extended thinking chains, keeping latency and quota low. Escalate to copy-high only for flagship positioning or high-stakes external communications.
lanes.origin: user 2026-10-30: Argon for copy and human-touch work; medium default, high only for high-stakes copy

lanes.match: High-stakes copy only: flagship App Store or landing-page positioning, launch narratives, and sensitive executive, customer, or partner communications.
lanes.reason: Reserve gemini-4-argon-high when multi-constraint positioning, audience tradeoffs, or sensitive tone justify higher deliberation cost.
lanes.origin: user 2026-10-30: reserve Argon high for high-stakes copy

lanes.match: Browser automation, iOS/Android simulator driving, desktop/GUI interaction, visual QA flows, and interactive app or device dogfooding.
lanes.reason: GPT-6.1 Terra is purpose-tuned for computer use and GUI/simulator/browser driving. Medium effort tracks multi-step UI state and repro evidence reliably without burning high/max reasoning quota on every action-observe turn. If Codex hits weekly reserve, hold GUI/simulator work as BLOCKED: quota unless the owner steers an override.
lanes.origin: user 2026-10-30: route browser/simulator/desktop/GUI-driving and device-dogfood tasks to GPT-6.1 Terra

lanes.match: Clear-spec non-UI implementation, schema/validator/wiring, 1-3 files, migrations, mechanical sweeps, and data analysis; excludes user-facing UI/API design (judgment) and copy (copy).
lanes.reason: GPT-6.1-Sol is the current Codex coding workhorse. Pin both -m gpt-6.1-sol and model_reasoning_effort=medium so launches do not inherit ~/.codex/config.toml defaults (currently gpt-6.1-terra at low). Escalate to judgment (claude-opus-5-5) on gate failure.
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-02 & 2026-10-30: route mechanical to current Codex workhorse (GPT-6.1-Sol)

lanes.match: Small crisp-spec mechanical work: 1-3 files, renames, mop-ups, boilerplate wiring, or straightforward edits where fast turnaround matters.
lanes.reason: GPT-6-Luna handles small, unambiguous mechanical tasks at low cost and latency. Gate hard and escalate to mechanical (gpt-6.1-sol) on any ambiguity; never eligible for review.
lanes.origin: 2026-10-30 model refresh: GPT-6-Luna small mechanical lane

lanes.match: Critical-path mechanical chunk blocking a wave where latency matters more than Codex credit burn.
lanes.reason: Codex fast tier on GPT-6.1-Sol (~1.5x speed at ~2.5x credit burn) - opt in per blocking chunk only, never bulk; ChatGPT sign-in only.
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-02: fast-lane variant, updated to GPT-6.1-Sol

lanes.match: Cross-engine mechanical parallelism when Codex lanes are saturated, taste-floor UI implementation when Opus is saturated, or mechanical fallback when Codex weekly quota is at or below FLEET_CODEX_RESERVE.
lanes.reason: Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort provides a funded non-Codex mechanical build lane (and UI taste floor) when Codex hits weekly reserve or needs cross-engine parallelism; escalate to judgment (claude-opus-5-5) on gate failure.
lanes.origin: 2026-10-30 model refresh: Sonnet 5.5 non-Codex mechanical lane

lanes.match: Reactor-subtle, security-critical, multi-file implementation, user-facing UI implementation, public API design, and complex architecture seams; excludes design-plan authoring (Astra) and copywriting (Argon).
lanes.reason: Opus 5.5 at high effort handles deep unsupervised implementation, user-facing UI/API taste, and subtle invariants without max-effort token waste; always pin --model and --effort explicitly.

lanes.match: Critical-path judgment chunk blocking a wave where latency matters more than cost.
lanes.reason: Claude fast mode on Opus 5.5 via --settings flagSettings (no --fast CLI flag); billed higher while active and subject to org/cooldown availability.
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-02: fast-lane variant, updated to Claude Opus 5.5

lanes.match: Independent frontier review of high-stakes plans, reports, and diffs, plus disputed gate tiebreaks only; design and plan authoring route to design-plan (Astra). Never a build or dogfood lane.
lanes.reason: Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) is the Mythos-class tier above Opus 5.5; medium effort matches ~/.claude/settings.json and avoids excessive burn. Follow the Argon-first review lane when eligible and use a review-only (-p) launch without permission bypass.
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-12: fable review-only; user 2026-09-08: design plans moved to Astra; 2026-10-30: Fable 5.1

lanes.match: Headless CLI/API tracer-bullet smoke or non-GUI dogfood fallback when Codex weekly quota is at reserve; route GUI, browser, simulator, desktop, and device dogfood to computer-use (gpt-6.1-terra) first.
lanes.reason: Interactive app/GUI/simulator dogfood routes to computer-use (GPT-6.1 Terra). Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort handles non-GUI tracer smoke (escalate reactor-subtle smoke to claude-opus-5-5).
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-16 & 2026-10-30: Terra leads GUI/device dogfood; Sonnet 5.5 covers headless smoke

lanes.match: Co-orchestrator watchdog over the primary orchestrator, external rotation trigger-holder, and advisory TANDEM-JUDGE on autonomous/overnight runs (skip short attended runs).
lanes.reason: Second frontier perspective from a different engine than the orchestrator (read-only + advisory; orchestrator keeps gate/merge), capped at high effort (never max). When Codex hits weekly reserve and the orchestrator is Claude, run tandem on Argon at medium effort (agy --dangerously-skip-permissions --model gemini-4-argon-medium — 10-minute watchdog/context checks and terse TANDEM-JUDGE verdicts do not warrant argon-high latency or quota burn per sweep); use claude-opus-5-5 (--effort medium) only when the orchestrator is non-Claude.
lanes.origin: user 2026-07-16 & 2026-09-06: cross-engine tandem watchdog capped at high effort

lanes.match: Review triage, concrete repo verification gates, and merge under main-merge claim.
